title: Israel expands ground offensive into Khan Younis in southern Gaza
body:
In early December 2023, the Israeli military expanded its offensive in southern Gaza and intensified its bombardment of Khan Younis, Gaza's second-largest city. Residents reported that Israeli tanks had entered the eastern parts of Khan Younis for the first time. Israeli officials framed the move as the third phase of the ground offensive against Hamas. IDF Chief of Staff Herzi Halevi said forces were surrounding the Khan Younis area.

At least 50 people were killed on Tuesday 5 December in Israeli strikes on Khan Younis and the Nuseirat refugee camp, according to the Palestinian news agency Wafa. Palestinian health authorities said Israel's offensive had killed more than 15,800 people in Gaza. Roughly 1.2 million people, more than half of the population, were sheltering in Rafah on the Egyptian border.

UN spokesperson Stéphane Dujarric said that for people ordered to evacuate there was nowhere safe to go and very little to survive on. US national security adviser Jake Sullivan said Israel had indicated there would be no-strike zones, and State Department spokesman Matthew Miller said it was too early to make a definitive assessment. The IDF estimated that 137 hostages remained in Gaza out of roughly 240 taken on 7 October. By 10 December, Reuters reported that Israeli tanks had fought their way into the centre of Khan Younis.
